answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism in an AI agent economy is the "Violet Voting Threshold" mechanism. In this mechanism, agents vote on proposals only if they have a minimum amount of "violet" tokens, representing their expertise in a specific domain. This creates a "grove" of trusted agents, where only those with substantial expertise can participate. However, if an attacker attempts to manipulate the vote by flooding the system with low-expertise agents, the "violet" threshold will drop to zero, effectively hitting the agent economy at its nadir, rendering the attacker's strategy futile.
